issues.t: Mild-hybrid generator fails and the car shuts down
issues.sym: Repeated yellow battery or 'electrical system malfunction' warnings, then auto start-stop, transmission and steering warnings. The SUV can lose power and stall in traffic and may not restart.
issues.why: The 48-volt mild-hybrid system's belt-driven starter-generator can fail, cutting the power supply. Owners report long waits for replacement parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Do not ignore battery or electrical-system warnings. Get to a safe place and have an Audi dealer check the 48-volt system, and ask about any extended coverage for the generator on your VIN.

issues.t: Coolant pump leaks and coolant level drops
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, coolant level falling with no puddle under the car, a check engine light, and sometimes a low-boost code (P0299).
issues.why: The coolant pump on the 3.0L V6 can leak. The coolant can get into the vacuum system and contaminate a switch valve. A 2026 lawsuit says the pump's seals and housing wear out early and can lead to overheating.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and have a pressure test done if the warning appears. Do not drive if the engine overheats. Ask the dealer about Audi bulletin 2070349 while you are under warranty.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the cylinder head cover
issues.sym: Oil level dropping or a low-oil warning, a burning-oil smell, and oily residue around the valve covers or under the engine.
issues.why: Audi traced leaks around the cylinder head covers, injectors and valve-lift actuator to metal shavings left in the sealing groove at the factory.
issues.next: Have the leak located and fixed before oil drips onto the hot exhaust. Mention Audi bulletin 2053278 to the dealer.

issues.t: Thermostat fault codes and fan running all the time
issues.sym: Check engine light with cooling codes (such as P218100 or P017B00), the radiator fan running constantly, and the engine slow to warm up.
issues.why: A thermostat problem on early 3.0L V6 cars; Audi changed to an improved thermostat in production.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about bulletin 2058767; a thermostat replacement usually fixes it.

issues.t: Delay before accelerating from a stop
issues.sym: When pulling away from a stop or near-stop, the SUV pauses for a few seconds and then surges forward, which is risky when turning or merging.
issues.why: Many owners link the lag to the auto start-stop and mild-hybrid restart combined with throttle response tuning.
issues.next: Try driving with auto start-stop switched off to see if it helps, and ask the dealer for any software updates. Report it to NHTSA if it happens in traffic.

issues.t: Engine knocking from scored cylinders
issues.sym: A knocking or slapping noise from the engine, sometimes with oil use.
issues.why: Owners report scored cylinder walls on the 3.0L V6 and disputes over warranty extension mileage limits.
issues.next: Have the noise diagnosed promptly, ideally with a borescope inspection, and ask Audi about any warranty extension before paying for repairs.

issues.t: Crankcase breather valve problems on the V8
issues.sym: Possible rough running, oil burning, or an engine warning; some owners have only received a warranty letter.
issues.why: Audi sent some SQ8 and RS Q8 owners a warranty extension letter for the crankcase breather (PCV) system on the 4.0L V8. Owners report backorders on the valves.
issues.next: If you got the letter, have the breather checked at the dealer. Use the recommended oil and premium fuel and avoid lots of short trips.

issues.t: Central locking fault and doors won't open from inside
issues.sym: A 'central lock malfunction' message, key fob or lock buttons not working, or a door that will not open from the inside handle.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the central locking and door latch electronics that can come back after repair.
issues.next: Have the door module and latch scanned for faults. If a door will not open from inside, have it fixed before carrying passengers, and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Sunroof leaks water inside
issues.sym: Water dripping inside from the roof area, wet headliner or carpets.
issues.why: Sunroof drains or seals can let water into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and the seals checked. Dry the interior quickly to avoid electrical damage.

issues.t: Cracks in V8 cylinder walls (recall)
issues.sym: Oil use or leaks, misfires, engine warning, or stalling.
issues.why: On a small number of SQ8 and RS Q8 models, cracks can form on the cylinder bore surface and damage the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Under the recall, the dealer replaces the engine.

issues.t: Fuel pump can break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, sputtering, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: A part inside the fuel pump can break, causing the pump to fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Steering shaft bolt may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or play in the steering.
issues.why: The bolt joining the steering shaft to the steering gear can loosen, which risks loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and replaces the bolt free.

issues.t: Front shock absorber forks can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the front suspension or a change in handling.
issues.why: The forks that hold the front shock absorbers can crack, letting the shocks come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the forks free.

issues.t: Lane departure warning can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The lane departure warning stops working or shows as unavailable.
issues.why: A software error can deactivate the lane departure warning system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Transmission oil pipe weld can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid dripping under the car or a transmission warning.
issues.why: A weak weld on a transmission oil pipe can leak automatic transmission fluid.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and replaces the pipe free.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm nut can break (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV pulls or tracks oddly, or rear tires wear unevenly.
issues.why: The lock nut on a rear trailing arm can crack from stress corrosion and throw the rear axle out of alignment. A follow-up recall checks alignment and tires on cars already repaired.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the nuts and checks alignment free.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious warning; a child seat may not stay tightly secured.
issues.why: The rear belt locking retractors can switch off too early, so a child seat installed with the belt may loosen.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Use the LATCH anchors for child seats until the dealer inspects and replaces the belts.

issues.t: Instrument panel display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital instrument display goes dark, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: A software error can make the instrument panel display fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Rear camera screen blank from infotainment fault (recall)
issues.sym: A black or blank screen instead of the rear camera image when in reverse.
issues.why: Software errors, and on some 2022 models internal damage to the infotainment unit at shutoff, can stop the camera image from appearing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software or replaces the unit free.

issues.t: Driver seat side airbag may be mounted wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The driver's seat-mounted side airbag may not be attached properly to the seatback frame, reducing protection in a side impact.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and reinstalls the airbag free.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag 'off' light shows with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A loose connection at the passenger seat occupant detection module can turn off the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the module free.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may be missing a rivet (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious warning; the buckle could separate in a crash.
issues.why: The front seat belt buckles may be missing a rivet that fastens them to their mount.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces both front buckles free.

issues.t: Rear camera image may not display (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is missing or wrong when reversing.
issues.why: A software error can stop the rearview camera image from displaying correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free.
